time_convention: t = frame / 24; frame = round(t*24); frame 0 at t=0
units: pixels (image coords, x right, y down) and seconds; no metric scale recorded

camera.evidence: phase correlation of rows 200-560 (wall/rail, never crossed by the ball) vs frame 0: |shift| < 0.01 px in every frame
camera.perspective: side view of a horizontal lane; all scene structures are horizontal bands with constant row over the full width (lane top edge at y=639 for every column) -> no visible horizontal perspective/tilt; camera looks slightly down onto the lane top (ball contact point y~688 lies inside the white lane band 640-737). Motion is a horizontal line at constant image row: treat as planar, one m/px scale.

objects.name: ball
objects.description: dark blue marbled sphere (sole moving object), rolls left to right on the white lane
objects.partially_visible_frames: 9-16 entering at left edge (frames 17-18 flagged because the trailing shadow touches x=0; ball itself is fully inside), 93-96 leaving at right edge (93 flagged by shadow/blur only)
objects.reference_point: centre of the fitted circle (cx, cy) = sphere centre = object origin

diameter_px.note: circle fit to mask rim above the shadow (frames 19-92); mid-video frames 40-80 give 80.2-81.8; frames 19-33 and 82-92 fit up to 84-85 (texture/blur at rim). Vertical extent of the mask at frame 48: y 607..688 (~81-82 px). Edge-cut frames use fixed r=40.6.

objects.length_px: = diameter (sphere): ~81 px; width and height likewise ~81 px

image_row_cy_px.note: cy wobbles +-1.5 px with ~10-frame period (rim texture of the rolling ball); real vertical motion is nil -> motion is purely horizontal

per_frame_step_px.note: ball speeds up throughout: pixel step grows from ~8 px/frame (frame 10) to ~29 px/frame (frame 95); increase is fastest early and slows later. Per-frame noise of cx ~ +-1 px.
